page0.text:
In that instant...
I deploy the strongest weapon out of all the items I've ever replicated.
But it won't even work as a shield against what is presented before me.
The sword of rupture.
The mysterious sword cuts through the wind, annihilates six Noble Phantasms, and severs my body.

page1.text:
It's disappearing.
My circuit gets disconnected, and the magical energy from Tohsaka has nowhere to go but back.
"Da...mn..."

page2.text:
I curse at my inadequacy.
I knew I was inexperienced. But I seriously curse at myself for never really thinking of the implications or how that would affect me.
Why do I have so few Magic Circuits?
If only I had a little more...
If only I had a little more, and reached beyond that darkness a bit...I could have fought like him...

page3.text:
I fall to the ground.
I can't soften the impact and I fly dozens of meters away, falling violently on my back.

page4.text:
There's no pain from the impact.
I've lost all sensation.
Even my mind goes white and blank.
Right before I head toward death...
My last thought is how amazed I am that my limbs are still attached.

page5.text: "This ends here. A fake will always be a fake. You cannot save anyone."

page6.text:
My heartbeat gets weaker.
My lungs are not moving, and my trachea is frozen.

page7.text:
"Sparing Archer would have afforded me more amusement.
He was also a fraud, but at least his principles were not uncultured."

page8.text:
The fact that I can't see isn't because my eyes are damaged.
Right now, everything inside me is messed up, and my body has ceased to function properly.
Maybe I would consider that to be fortunate.
I've forgotten all sensation of pain, so I should be able to die easily at this rate...

page9.text: "Ah. I remember now. He said your ideal is a borrowed one. How can someone who has not created a single thing from his own accord think he can accomplish anything?"

page10.text:
I can't...let that happen.
Even if the pain causes me to be brain-dead if I come to my senses, I tell myself I need to regain consciousness and stand up.
My deeply rooted psyche is pointing to a certain place and telling me something.

page11.text:
"A hero of justice? A world where no one gets hurt?
You say such ridiculous things. There is no such world where happiness can be preserved without harming others.
Humans are basically beasts that cannot enjoy their life without sacrifice. The pretense of equality is nothing more than drivel by the weak who cannot face darkness.
Mongrel. Your ideal is just an excuse to cover up ugliness."

page12.text:
...
I raise my arm, even though it shouldn't be able to move.
My body is on the ground and my consciousness is on the brink of death.
I raise my arm to grab on to something...like I did on that fateful day.

page13.text:
I don't know what's funny, but someone's laughing.
The high pitched laughter that assaults my ears sounded like everyone in the entire world was laughing.

page14.text:
A fake wish.
A borrowed ideal.
That dream won't come true, someone sneers.

page15.text:
Yeah...they're right.
These thoughts of mine are borrowed.
I just admired the wish to help someone because it was beautiful.
There's nothing that came from me.
I was always driven by this curse-like obsession that my body needed to be for someone else.

page16.text:
That's why it's fake.
Such hypocrisy will save nothing in the end.
First of all, I don't even know what needs to be saved.

page17.text:
But...
But I also still feel that's beautiful.

page18.text:
That concept did not come from me.
I just saw someone save someone else, and mimicked it.
On that day, I was empty inside.
Everyone died indiscriminately, and I couldn't save anyone.
I couldn't suppress my terror at that sight that was unraveling before me, and I had no choice but to resign myself to the fact that humans were weak.

page20.text:
That's why I admired that ideal.
I cried at the preciousness of it because I didn't have it myself.
Is that wrong?
Is it fake because it's not my own feelings?
Is it wrong for that wish to come true if it's fake?

page21.text: No. I don't think it's wrong.

page23.text:
I don't care if it's fake.
Even unattainable ideals just need to be fulfilled.
It was a dream that couldn't be granted from the start. An unreachable utopia.

page24.text:
Then, even if Shirou Emiya is a fake...
The thing that is there is undeniably real.

page26.text:
I know I can't save everything.
I know that there's no salvation without sacrifice.
Now that I'm an adult, I understand that's reality.
Despite knowing that such a thing was only an ideal, I continued to seek for it.

page27.text:
It doesn't end when someone gets hurt.
Even if the best outcome is for someone to get hurt in order to save many, I'm still going to seek a version of happiness where nobody gets hurt.
There's no justice in this world...
The reality is that people keep dying for nothing...
But I don't think resigning to that idea is right!

page28.text: And in the end, he reached this place.

page29.text:
What he believes...
What he believed...
He said they were all hypocrisy.

page30.text:
But the one who said that followed through on his hypocrisy till the end.
...Knowing that, I can keep going.
Even if I borrowed his ideals...even if I'm going to stay a fake...I don't care.
I don't have such complicated feelings that I have to worry about too much in the first place.

page31.text:
I thought to myself on the hill of swords.
If I could save just the world that I can see, I'll fight for it.
I didn't even have to think about it.
My world is small.
This small world is all I have ever been able to create.

page32.text:
That's right.
This body of mine is made of solid swords.

page33.text:
Yeah. That's why I'll be able to endure most things.
I can stick to my dreams until the very end.
Even the wear and tear over the years.
And even if at the end...
None of what I sought was there.

page35.text:
I get up.
The moment I regain consciousness, my limbs move.
My body still moves after I get up with great force.
It's a wonder I'm not only alive but able to stand up after that sword's blow... but it doesn't matter.

page36.text:
If I'm alive, there must be a reason why.
It's something that I just have no control over.

page37.text:
"Did you put up a shield right before? I may have been reluctant to use my sword, but it should still have been fatal.
I knew you were persistent, boy."

page38.text: "You were reluctant? Heh. Why would you hold back when you have mounds of weapons at bay?"

page39.text:
I steady my breath while keeping my distance.
I know how to do it now.
I'm sure I can do it with Tohsaka's backup.
The problem would be my casting time.
I may have memorized it, but I don't know how fast I can get it to work for me unless I try.

page40.text:
"Hmph. Only the supreme ruler is allowed to use that sword.
I showed it to you for my amusement, but it is not something to be used against a mongrel like you.
The only person who has the right to exchange blows with Ea is Saber.
I would have been unable to face Saber had I used it on a fake like you."

page41.text:
Numerous Noble Phantasms appear.
But all of them are third-rate weapons.
After seeing the sword I just saw, the difference is obvious.

page42.text:
But those weapons are still not to be taken lightly.
Normally they would be more than enough to kill me.
The difference in our strength has not changed.
Even though I miraculously survived that last attack, I'm no match against that Servant with just my Projection.

page43.text:
"Oh? Are you done playing pretend? So you've finally realized your efforts are useless...
Then disappear without a trace. I will not leave a single piece of cranium that makes you a fake!"

page44.text:
The floating Noble Phantasms are deployed.
But then...
"Shirou!"
A gust of blue wind intervenes between us.

page45.text:
"Saber!?"
Gilgamesh instantly jumps back.
Even Gilgamesh is cautious against Saber.
Seeing as his swordsmanship is inferior, he probably wants to avoid hand-to-hand combat with Saber.

page46.text:
"I am relieved. Are you all right, Shirou?
I apologize for my delay. I shall take over now. Please stand back, Shirou."

page47.text: "No. I'm going to take care of Gilgamesh alone. You're the one who's going to step back, Saber."

page49.text:
"Wh-what are you saying, Shirou!?
Do you intend to fight him in your current state? No. A mage cannot contend against Servants in the first place. You should know that."

page50.text:
"Yeah. But he and I are an exception. Believe me.
I'm sure I can beat him."
Saber gasps.
Saber is surprised because she believes what I'm saying.

page51.text:
"I want you to quickly get to the back of the compound. Tohsaka's trying to stop the grail on her own. But you're the only one who can destroy that thing."
...
A few seconds...no, not even a second passed.
After she tightly closed her eyes once...

page52.text:
"I wish you luck. I will be sure to aid Rin."
She says exactly what I want to hear, and steps away from Gilgamesh.

page53.text:
The silver armor turns away.
"Saber."
I call out to her just once.

page54.text:
"I couldn't save you..."
And I say it.
I'm going to try to tell her on behalf of the times I spent with her and the times he spent thinking of her...

page55.text:
"I don't think that Holy Grail is the one you seek.
That's why you should take a good look at it. So you won't make a mistake next time."
"...Shirou?"

page56.text:
"Sorry. I can't put it into words well. I don't think I was worthy to be your Master.
That's why..."
I couldn't even find out what she really wanted.

page57.text:
"That is not true. Shirou. You are my Master."
"...Saber."
"I will fulfill my duty as a Servant. If there is anything you want to tell me, we shall talk afterwards."

page58.text:
She runs off without turning back.
Her gallant appearance is like a gust of wind.

page59.text:
Saber left.
Without the slightest doubt, she believed my words when I said I would beat my opponent, and left to save Tohsaka.

page61.text:
From here on, there's no room for hesitation.
All I need to do is to defeat the enemy in front of me.

page63.text:
"Are you sane? You just let go of your one chance at victory so you can save that girl!?
You fool. Acts of self-sacrifice are nothing but falsehood. If you still do not realize that, then you are a bona fide hypocrite.
Ah yes...I'll praise you just on that front, boy."

page64.text:
His Noble Phantasms deploy.
There're less than thirty of them.
If I want to block them, I'll just have to create them.

page65.text:
"An imitation...a hypocrite, huh? Yeah, that doesn't sound bad. It's true: I am a faker."
I raise one of my arms.
I close one eye and turn my mind to look within.

page66.text:
"Hn?"
"I had it all wrong. My Projection wasn't making swords. I'm not that skilled to begin with."

page67.text:
That's right.
Tohsaka told me this. I can only use one kind of magecraft.
Strengthening and Projection are just by-products of what I actually do.

page68.text:
"That's right. There's only one thing I can do, and that's to give shape to what's in my heart."
I turn.
I grab my outstretched right arm with my left hand and glare at Gilgamesh.

page69.text:
"I am the bone of my sword..."
I say the spell.
Casting is only a method of suggestion to change oneself.
These words were naturally there to connect me.

page70.text:
"Well. That is enough of this nonsense."
Numerous Noble Phantasms get released.
I create.
That's why I had one eye open.
I drag out a shield from the hill to block the oncoming Noble Phantasms.

page71.text:
"Gngh...!"
The swarm of swords strike wildly.
The shield is Shirou Emiya...myself.
The seven petal shield cracks, and my body chips away with every fracture.

page72.text:
"Steel is my body, and fire is...
my blood."
There's only one place I need to reach.
The power that surges forth immediately fills me to capacity.

page73.text:
"Wha...t!?"
What is he so surprised about?
Is he shocked that his treasure can't even penetrate through my single shield? Or is he surprised by the rush of magical energy?

page74.text:
"I have created over a thousand blades.
Unaware of loss.
Nor aware of gain."

page75.text:
It's going to break.
The surging magical energy can't be suppressed.
Ten units of magical energy filling a single Magic Circuit break the foundation to find release.
"I cannot break through...!?"
My blood flows backwards.
The shield is full of holes.
Even if his Noble Phantasms do not reach me, my body is full of holes already.
And yet...
"Withstood pain to create weapons.
Waiting for one's arrival."
Magical energy rages out of control.
But I don't care.
My body is a circuit that solely exists to use a certain magecraft, and that magecraft alone.
So there should be something beyond that.
There should be something beyond that if I can't make it with this circuit.

page76.text:
No. Even now it's there.
It's just not visible.
There were no circuit limitations from the very beginning.
If what was preventing it was not a wall, but darkness...
Then the limit is somewhere beyond the darkness.

page77.text: "I have no regrets. This is the only path."

page78.text: Ten units of magical energy filling a single Magic Circuit break the foundation to find release, and I will use one hundred circuits to take in a thousand units of magical energy.

page79.text: "My whole life was unlimited blade works."

page80.text:
I say its True Name.
In that instant...
Everything shatters and regenerates.

page81.text:
Flames rush.
The fire becomes a wall that creates a boundary, and changes the world.
A wasteland follows.
A hill with countless swords in disarray reveals itself before me.

page82.text:
...
How does this place look to that guy?
The golden Servant simply stands there with a seething look on his face and confronts his enemy.

page83.text:
"That's right. I don't make swords.
I create a world that contains infinite swords.
This is the only magecraft allowed to me."

page84.text:
A desolate world.
A graveyard where there are no living creatures...only swords.
In this world where swords get replicated just by looking directly at them, every sword in existence is here.

page85.text:
This is Shirou Emiya's world.
A Reality Marble.
The greatest forbidden magecraft that materializes the caster's mental world.
This is the Heroic Spirit Emiya's Noble Phantasm, and the only weapon I possess.

page86.text:
Everything is here, and nothing is here.
That's why it's called Unlimited Blade Works.
As someone who lived his whole life as a sword, this is the only definite and tangible answer he was able to obtain.

page87.text:
"A Reality Marble. So this is your ability!"
I take a step forward.
Surrounding me are the swords that were floating behind him earlier.

page88.text:
"Don't be surprised. These are all imitations.
Just as you said, they're all trifling objects."
I stretch out my arms.
The swords stuck in the ground come out easily, as if accepting me as their wielder.

page89.text:
"But you know what? There's no rule or reason a fake can't best the real thing.
If you're the real thing, then I'll surpass you completely and strike down your very existence."
I step forward.
In front of me is the Servant who possesses thousands of treasures.

page90.text: "Let's do this, King of Heroes. Do you have enough weapons in stock?"
